title: Mahalanobis Distance, Discriminant Analysis and MANOVA
breadcrumb: Module 8 · Multivariate Analysis · Mahalanobis distance, discriminant analysis and MANOVA
objectives: Calculate and interpret squared Mahalanobis distance.
Explain how covariance adjusts distance for scale and correlation.
Distinguish linear and quadratic discriminant analysis.
Explain the purpose of MANOVA and recognise its four common criteria.

prereq.name: Mean vectors and covariance matrices
prereq.why: Mahalanobis distance measures displacement relative to covariance geometry.

prereq.name: Matrix inverse and quadratic forms
prereq.why: The distance is a quadratic form involving the inverse covariance matrix.

prereq.name: Multivariate normal distribution
prereq.why: Classical discriminant methods and MANOVA are commonly introduced under normal models.

traps: Use Σ⁻¹, not Σ, in the Mahalanobis quadratic form.
D² is squared distance; take a square root only when D is requested.
LDA assumes a common within-group covariance matrix.
MANOVA tests group mean response vectors jointly.
A small Wilks' lambda is not itself a p-value.

sheet: If X~Nₚ(μ,Σ), with μ and Σ known, then D²~χ²ₚ.
LDA: multivariate normal groups with a common covariance matrix; linear boundary.
QDA: group-specific covariance matrices; boundaries generally quadratic.
MANOVA tests H₀: μ₁=…=μg for a vector-valued response.
Common criteria: Wilks' lambda, Pillai's trace, Hotelling–Lawley trace and Roy's largest root.
With H and E denoting hypothesis and error sum-of-products matrices, Wilks' Λ=|E|/|E+H|.
Pillai's trace, Hotelling–Lawley trace and Roy's largest root are alternative MANOVA criteria.
Ordinary ANOVA has one response; MANOVA tests a response vector and its joint group effect.
cards: Joint test of mean response vectors
tricks: Use D² directly for chi-square reference; do not take an unnecessary square root.
For diagonal Σ, sum squared deviations divided by corresponding variances.
LDA means pooled/common covariance; QDA means separate covariance matrices.
Several dependent variables and a group effect suggest MANOVA.
shortcuts: Check that Σ⁻¹ is p×p and the final quadratic form is scalar.
Identify common versus group-specific covariance before choosing LDA or QDA.
Distinguish a test statistic from its p-value.
remember: Mahalanobis distance adjusts for scale and correlation.
LDA shares covariance; QDA does not.
MANOVA compares group mean vectors jointly.

howto: For Mahalanobis distance, centre the observation, apply the inverse covariance matrix and form the quadratic product. For classification, identify whether covariance is shared across groups. For several response variables, formulate a joint MANOVA test of group mean vectors.

scenes.title: Distance in multivariate space
body: An observation with p variables is a p×1 vector. Euclidean distance treats all coordinates as if they had the same scale and were unrelated.
Real variables may have different variances and may be correlated. The covariance matrix describes this scale and dependence structure.
Mahalanobis distance uses the covariance matrix to adjust displacement from a reference centre.

items.ask: What is on the diagonal of a covariance matrix?
refresh: The jth diagonal entry is the variance of variable j. It measures spread along that coordinate.
Off-diagonal entries are covariances. They describe how pairs of variables vary together and determine the orientation of the data cloud.

items.ask: Which matrix appears in the standard Mahalanobis formula?
refresh: The inverse covariance matrix scales deviations by their variability and accounts for correlations.
Using the covariance matrix rather than its inverse would not give the standard Mahalanobis distance.

items.ask: What is the dimension of the final quadratic form?
refresh: The sample mean vector is formed by averaging each coordinate across all n observations. If each observation is p×1, the mean vector is also p×1; its jth coordinate is the ordinary sample mean of variable j. It provides the centre from which multivariate deviations are measured.

In the multivariate normal likelihood, differentiating with respect to the unknown mean vector gives the sample mean vector as the maximum-likelihood estimate. Each observation is then centred by subtracting this vector before the covariance matrix is estimated. This centring is essential: using uncentred observations would mix location with spread.

ask.q: Why can Euclidean distance mislead when variables are strongly correlated?
ask.nudge: Think about the long and short axes of an elliptical data cloud.

scenes.title: Distance from a data cloud
body: Imagine observations forming a long tilted ellipse. Moving along its long axis is common; moving the same raw distance across its narrow axis is unusual.
Mahalanobis distance accounts for the ellipse's scale and orientation. It measures displacement relative to the covariance structure.
A point that appears far away in raw units may still be typical when its direction follows the natural spread of the data.

scenario.title: Height and weight
body: Suppose height and weight are measured for a group of adults. These variables tend to be positively correlated, so the data cloud is elongated along a rising diagonal. A person who is tall and correspondingly heavy may lie far from the coordinate-wise average in raw units but still follow the usual population pattern. Another person with the same height but unusually low weight may depart sharply from that pattern.

Mahalanobis distance evaluates the displacement using the inverse covariance matrix. The covariance structure downweights directions in which observations naturally vary widely and gives more weight to unusual directions. This is why it can identify multivariate outliers that are not obvious from separate one-variable comparisons.
scenario.q: What extra information does Mahalanobis distance use?
scenario.answer: The covariance structure, including variances and correlations.

ask.q: What happens to the distance if centimetres are converted to metres and covariance is transformed consistently?
ask.nudge: The covariance adjustment makes the measure invariant to nonsingular linear coordinate changes.

blocks.body: D²(x,μ)=(x−μ)′Σ⁻¹(x−μ), where Σ is positive definite.
D² is nonnegative. The distance itself is D=√D².
If X~Nₚ(μ,Σ), with μ and Σ known, then D²(X,μ)~χ²ₚ.
If μ and Σ are estimated from the same sample, do not automatically apply the known-parameter chi-square result; the reference distribution changes.

blocks.body: Given an observed vector x, assign it to one of g known groups using group distributions or discriminant scores.
Classical LDA assumes multivariate normal groups with a common covariance matrix Σg=Σ. Comparing group scores leaves a linear function of x.
QDA allows group-specific covariance matrices Σg. The inverse covariance and determinant terms vary by group, so boundaries are generally quadratic.
Use LDA when a common covariance assumption is reasonable. QDA is more flexible but estimates more covariance parameters.

ask.q: Which method has a linear decision boundary under the classical normal model?
ask.nudge: It is the method with a common covariance matrix.

scenes.title: Choose the classifier
scenes.problem: Two multivariate normal populations have different mean vectors but are assumed to share the same covariance matrix. Which classical discriminant method fits?
hints: A common covariance leads to a linear discriminant score.
Remember that LDA pools the within-group covariance information.

solution.why: The groups share one covariance matrix.
The shared covariance causes quadratic terms to cancel in the comparison of normal discriminant scores.

scenario.title: A second classification study
body: A bank builds a classifier using two financial ratios to distinguish low-risk and high-risk borrowers. Initial plots suggest that both groups have different spreads and different covariance patterns: one group is widely dispersed along a diagonal, while the other is more compact and nearly circular. A single pooled covariance matrix may conceal this important group-specific structure.

QDA can represent this difference by estimating a covariance matrix separately for each group. This flexibility comes at a cost: more parameters must be estimated, so a sufficiently large sample in each group is important. The choice between LDA and QDA is therefore a modelling decision, not merely a preference for a more complicated formula.
scenario.q: Which alternative allows each group its own covariance matrix?
scenario.teaser: When a shared covariance assumption fails

ask.q: What is one cost of QDA?
ask.nudge: Consider the number of covariance parameters that must be estimated.

scenes.title: Spot the method-selection traps
scenes.intro: Decide whether each statement is correct.

items.claim: LDA assumes a common within-group covariance matrix.
items.why: The classical LDA model uses a shared covariance matrix across groups.

items.claim: QDA assumes all groups have identical covariance matrices.
items.why: QDA allows each group to have its own covariance matrix.

items.claim: MANOVA is ordinary ANOVA on only one response variable.
items.why: MANOVA jointly analyses a vector of dependent responses.

items.claim: Mahalanobis distance is invariant under nonsingular linear coordinate changes when covariance is transformed consistently.
items.why: The covariance adjustment preserves the quadratic distance under such transformations.

ask.q: Which assumption separates LDA from QDA?
ask.nudge: Compare pooled and group-specific covariance matrices.

scenes.title: MANOVA and its common criteria
scenes.problem: Three groups are compared on two response variables. The question is whether their population mean response vectors are equal. Which method is appropriate?
hints: The null concerns the whole vector of means.
The four named criteria are alternative ways to summarise the H and E matrices.
scenes.check: Several responses and a joint group-mean hypothesis → MANOVA.

solution.math: Y is a vector with two responses.
solution.why: More than one dependent variable is analysed jointly.
The null states equality of the population mean response vectors.
MANOVA tests the group effect across the response vector simultaneously.

ask.nudge: It is a determinant ratio involving within-group error and total variation.

scenes.title: One-minute method selector
body: Mahalanobis distance measures covariance-adjusted separation: D²=(x−μ)′Σ⁻¹(x−μ).
LDA uses a common within-group covariance matrix; QDA permits group-specific covariance matrices.
MANOVA tests equality of group mean vectors when there are multiple response variables. Its common criteria are Wilks' lambda, Pillai's trace, Hotelling–Lawley trace and Roy's largest root.
This lesson is introductory: it focuses on definitions, interpretation and method selection rather than advanced derivations.

ask.q: Which method compares several groups on a vector of outcomes?
ask.nudge: It is the multivariate extension of ANOVA.
